posts.text:
Google's Gemini Omni Flash ran 6 edits on 1 photo before I called it serious

The pitch was conversational editing, so I stopped reading and started testing.

First, make a solid object see-through. It dropped the opacity and kept every edge of the original frame structure intact, nothing warped.

Then the easy one everyone has seen: swap an object out. 1 pass. So I pushed harder, dropped an animal into the room, reached over to pet it, and the model held the contact instead of melting the hand into fur.

Edit 4 is the post-production move most people actually want. The sofa was in the way, so I removed it. Empty floor, matched lighting, no smear where it sat.

Then the background. I animated it  the thing I had only seen in other testers' clips until I ran it myself. It moved.

Last, I swapped the water out and rebuilt the surface. 

That one needed the most prompting, but it landed.

6 tests, 6 passes. Not flawless a couple needed a second instruction, and it wants more abuse before I trust it on client work. But Google shipped this at I/O on May 19, and the floor is already this high.ʼ
